findings.title: Ingress hostname pattern alone cannot distinguish a Preview-target deployment of the dedicated project from a Production-target deployment of the same project
findings.counterexample: Vercel assigns the same '<name>-<9-char-id>-<team>.vercel.app' shape to deployment URLs regardless of target (preview or production); the regex only proves 'a deployment of this exact project/team', not 'a Preview-target deployment'. Preview/Production separation is enforced entirely by (a) ZAO_HOSTED_PREVIEW_RUNTIME being Preview-scoped in Vercel env config so phase6Requested() is false on Production, and (b) assertNoHostedPlatformContradiction rejecting VERCEL_ENV!=='preview' when that variable is present.
findings.impact: No exploitable gap given the two independent layers above (both verified in code and tests), but the hostname check should not be read as an independent Preview/Production discriminator. If the Preview-only env scoping were ever misconfigured on the Vercel project side, the hostname pattern alone would not catch it.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: No code change required; document explicitly (e.g. in hosted-preview-config.ts comments) that hostedPreviewRequestOrigin only enforces 'exact dedicated deployment, not a static alias/custom domain', and that Preview/Production separation is the job of the env-var capability scope plus assertNoHostedPlatformContradiction.
findings.required_proof: During the attempt5 predeploy gate, confirm via Vercel env metadata (already required by FINAL_HOSTED_REPAIR.md) that ZAO_HOSTED_PREVIEW_RUNTIME and ZAO_AVATAR_PHASE6 remain target=[preview] only, with Production env count 0.

scope_assessment: This review covers the supplied diff and full snapshot against the stated Owner authority replacing the old mandatory-identity gate with a positive Preview-only capability plus negative platform guards. The capability shape (parseHostedPreview), six least-privilege Neon roles/TLS proof, guest signing key, and exact read-only R2/expiry are all validated with exact-shape checks and are covered by targeted rejection tests (tests/unit/avatar-phase6.test.ts) for every field. Request-derived origin (HTTPS + Host=URL.host=x-vercel-deployment-url + immutable hostname regex) replaces the retired env-derived previewOrigin()/VERCEL_URL binding, matching the explicit authorization to stop treating VERCEL_URL/legacy marker as security-relevant. Peer identity uses only x-vercel-forwarded-for with no generic-header fallback, verified against spoofing attempts in tests. Guest and Avatar share the same origin/peer validator (vercelPreviewPeer -> hostedPreviewRequestOrigin) via GuestSecurity/avatarGuestSecurity.guard, confirmed by source reading of hosted-preview-runtime.ts's avatar boundary.
security_boundary_assessment: Production guestHandler security remains mandatory (guest-http.ts:13) and is invoked with simulation=false for the hosted path, keeping /checkout and /reconcile hard-503'd (PAYMENT_NOT_CONNECTED_CHARGE_DISABLED) regardless of target. NODE_ENV==='production' is used only as Next's build-mode signal to force this security gate and to prevent any local/public-runtime fallback (both the Guest route and guest-avatar-runtime.ts now explicitly short-circuit to null/503 under NODE_ENV=production when the Phase6 capability is absent), consistent with the explicit instruction that NODE_ENV must not be conflated with the actual Vercel Production target. assertNoHostedPlatformContradiction correctly treats VERCEL/VERCEL_ENV/VERCEL_TARGET_ENV/VERCEL_PROJECT_ID as optional vetoes (missing = permitted, present-and-wrong = PLATFORM_CONTRADICTION), and separately forbids SQUARE_/PAYMENT_/REFUND_/WEBHOOK_/DATABASE_URL/POSTGRES_URL/PGPASSWORD and any non-allowlisted ZAO_ key even when the value is empty or undefined. Fixed-stage diagnostics (hostedPreviewUnavailable) only ever emit {error, stage} from an allowlisted enum for both HostedPreviewStartupError and the new HostedPreviewBoundaryError, verified by tests injecting cause/stack/password fields that must not leak. The Avatar boundary carries no business-write capability (guard/load/reader only, R2 provider instantiated with a purge callback that always throws), keeping recommendation/HOLD/quote/checkout writes exclusively inside the pre-existing, unchanged GuestBookingService composition.
